properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Measured by the dev_storyflow fleet in one session, 2026-09-02, all four observed live:

| constructor | what it does with status |
| --- | --- |
| `add_decision` | lands `proposed` — and the brainstorm skill tells you to VERIFY it |
| `add_capability` | accepts an explicit `status` and honours it |
| `add_epoch` | lands `arrived` and does not take the field |
| `add_verification` | REJECTS the field (`unknown field 'status'`) and lands `planned`; recording a check that FAILED takes two calls |

Their point: *"for four sibling constructors there are four different contracts, and two of them require a second call to say the true thing. A design brain's whole value is that its statuses are true; the constructors should make the true thing the cheap thing."*

🛑 **ONE OF THEIR FOUR IS ALREADY ANSWERED AND THEIR PROPOSED FIX WOULD BE WRONG.** Wish #6 asks that `add_epoch` default to `planned`. But `plan_epoch` EXISTS for exactly that; `add_epoch`'s own description says it creates an epoch that "HAS HAPPENED" and names `plan_epoch` as the alternative; and `cap:planned-epochs` records the reasoning — *"The default is `arrived`, which is a record rather than a choice (`req:defaults-do-not-assert`): add_epoch's 27 call sites have only ever meant recording the point you are at."* Measured 2026-09-02: `find_tools` ranks `plan_epoch` FIRST for "create a milestone for work that has not started yet". The discovery surface worked and was not used. **Changing that default would break a reasoned decision to fix a discovery miss.**

⭐ SO THE REAL QUESTION IS NARROWER AND MORE INTERESTING: `add_decision` and `add_epoch` both follow `req:defaults-do-not-assert` and land at the not-yet-true end — and reach OPPOSITE-LOOKING answers, because for an epoch the not-asserting default IS `arrived` (you are recording where you are). `add_verification` refusing the field is a THIRD thing again, and has its own precedent: `fact:defect-add-verification-cannot-reach-its-own-fields` (2026-08-15) already records that constructor as too narrow, "half addressed".

OPTIONS, none preferred:
· **A — Accept `status` on every constructor, defaulting to the not-yet-done end.** Their wish #9. Uniform and cheap to describe. ⚠️ Collides with `req:defaults-do-not-assert` for epochs, where "not yet done" is the WRONG default — so it would have to carve out the one case that prompted the complaint.
· **B — Leave the defaults; make every constructor ECHO the status it assigned.** The half of their ask that survives the refutation above, and it is what they actually needed: *"Nothing warned me; I caught it only because I read the reply."* Costs one field.
· **C — Fix only `add_verification`**, the one with a standing recorded defect and no sibling tool to redirect to. Narrowest, and it closes a report already 18 days old.
· **D — Point the constructors at each other in prose**, as `add_epoch` already does for `plan_epoch`. ⚠️ `add_epoch` DID that and it did not work, which is evidence against prose as the whole answer.
· **E — Do nothing; the contracts differ because the node types differ.** ⚠️ Has to answer why four sibling calls in one workflow surprised an experienced reporter four times.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether `add_capability` honouring an explicit status is itself right, or whether it lets a caller assert `realized` with nothing built. Nobody has asked.
properties.name: OPEN — four sibling constructors answer "what status does this land in" four different ways. Is there one contract, and does defaults-do-not-assert already decide it?
properties.rationale:
Worth recording rather than acting on because the obvious repair — "make them all the same" — is refuted for the specific case that prompted it, and acting on the report as written would overturn `req:defaults-do-not-assert` and a documented 27-call-site rationale to fix something `find_tools` already answers.

What survives refutation is smaller and better: ECHO the status assigned (option B), and the standing `add_verification` narrowness (option C) which was recorded on 2026-08-15 and is still half-addressed.

CLOSED 2026-09-20 as ANSWERED, on Anthony's word. v0.65.0 settled the real complaint by letting every constructor of a status-carrying type state the status outright and name in its description what omitting it lands, so the case that prompted this — a constructor asserting more than the caller said — cannot arise. The surviving option, echoing back the status a call landed in, was declined as adding little once the caller can simply say it.
